title: Dal Makhani
subtitle: Slow-cooked black lentils in a rich, buttery tomato sauce
excerpt: Whole black lentils and kidney beans simmered for hours in a deep, spiced tomato sauce, finished with butter and cream. The long cook is what makes it.

recipe.sourceNotes: Dal makhani ('buttery lentils') originated in the Punjab region of India and was popularised through the Moti Mahal restaurant in Delhi in the 1950s. The dish is traditionally cooked overnight in a tandoor (clay oven), allowing the lentils to absorb the flavours of the sauce completely. The home version uses the hob or oven at low heat for several hours to replicate this effect. Whole urad dal (black lentils) are used, not split; they retain their shape but become very tender. The quantity of butter and cream is what gives the dish its characteristic richness. Reduce or replace with vegan alternatives if needed.

content.text: The lentils need at least 1 hour of simmering, and 2 hours is better. The longer they cook, the creamier the sauce becomes as the lentils break down slightly into the tomato base. Soak the lentils overnight if possible: they will cook more evenly and in less time. Add the butter and cream at the very end, off the heat or over the lowest possible flame.

items.preparation: soaked overnight; whole urad dal if available

content.text: Drain and rinse the soaked lentils. Cover with plenty of cold water in a large saucepan and bring to a boil. Simmer for 40 minutes until tender but not falling apart. Drain and reserve.
Heat the oil in a large heavy pan. Fry the cumin seeds for 30 seconds. Add the onion and cook for 12 minutes until deep golden. Add the garlic and ginger. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add the ground spices and tomato puree. Cook for 1 minute. Add the blended tinned tomatoes. Simmer for 10 minutes until the oil starts to separate from the sauce.
Add the cooked lentils, kidney beans, and 400 ml water. Season. Simmer on the lowest heat possible for at least 45 to 60 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce is thick and dark.
Stir in the butter and cream. Adjust the seasoning. Serve topped with fresh coriander alongside basmati rice and naan.
